records.app_claim: The last of Edward I’s Welsh castles, begun in 1295 after the rising of Madog ap Llywelyn. Money ran short and work petered out by the 1320s, leaving the towers below their planned height. The borough became the main port of Anglesey.
records.research_claim: Six inner towers and the south gatehouse never reached intended height; the unfinished profile is a material construction state, not a finished generic castle.

records.app_claim: The lowest crossing of the Clwyd. Edward the Elder founded a burh here in 921; it was Gruffudd ap Llywelyn’s seat until 1063; Robert of Rhuddlan raised a motte in 1073. Edward I began the present concentric castle in 1277 and issued the Statute of Rhuddlan here in 1284.
records.research_claim: The Clwyd was deepened and diverted to provide a ship supply route. Record this engineering work independently from castle construction.
